title: Gochujang Samgyeopsal
shortDescription: Pork belly is coated in a spicy-sweet gochujang marinade, then grilled over controlled heat until browned and safely cooked.
culturalContext: This is a contemporary spicy variation on grilled samgyeopsal using gochujang. Korean pork-belly preparations and marinades vary, so this draft does not present one universal formula.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}
equipment: Outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric grill

ingredients.preparation: cut across the grain into 6 mm / 1/4-inch slices

mixOrder: Whisk gochujang and soy sauce smooth.
Add rice syrup, garlic, ginger, and sesame oil.
marinadeOrSeasoning.marinationVessel: Nonreactive covered container kept at or below 40°F / 4°C
marinadeOrSeasoning.maximumPracticalMarinationWarning: Do not exceed 4 hours without test-cook approval; the salty marinade can alter texture.
marinadeOrSeasoning.reserveBeforeRawContactInstruction: Reserve any sauce for serving before it contacts raw pork.
marinadeOrSeasoning.rawContactDiscardOrReboilInstruction: Discard raw-contact marinade; do not brush it onto cooked meat unless separately brought to a full boil under an approved process.
substitutions: Use only verified gluten-free gochujang and tamari for a gluten-free adaptation.

instructions.heading: Prepare safely
instructions.action: Trim and portion the skinless pork belly slab on a dedicated raw-meat board, then wash hands.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep raw pork and its juices away from ready-to-eat foods.

instructions.heading: Mix the seasoning
instructions.action: Stir gochujang, soy sauce, rice syrup, garlic, ginger, and sesame oil until smooth.
instructions.safetyNote: Reserve any table sauce before raw-pork contact.

instructions.heading: Marinate under refrigeration
instructions.action: Coat the pork evenly, cover, and marinate for 1 hour in the refrigerator.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Each slice has a thin, even coating.
instructions.safetyNote: Never marinate pork at room temperature.

instructions.heading: Preheat the grill
instructions.action: Preheat a clean outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric grill and lightly oil the grate.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The grate is hot and clean.
instructions.safetyNote: Do not use a fuel-burning grill indoors; follow the appliance manufacturer’s ventilation instructions.

instructions.heading: Grill and verify
instructions.action: Shake off excess marinade and grill in one layer, turning often to prevent scorching, until browned and at least 145°F / 63°C.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The thickest pieces reach at least 145°F / 63°C on a calibrated thermometer.
instructions.safetyNote: Use clean tongs after the final turn and never place cooked pork on the raw-meat platter.

instructions.heading: Rest and serve
instructions.action: Transfer to a clean platter and rest 3 minutes before slicing or serving.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Juices settle during the full 3-minute rest.
instructions.safetyNote: Whole cuts of pork require 145°F / 63°C followed by a 3-minute rest.

grillSetup: Use an outdoor grill or a manufacturer-approved indoor electric grill on a heat-safe surface. Preheat, clean, and lightly oil the grate; keep raw and cooked zones and utensils separate.
targetInternalTemperature: 145°F / 63°C in the thickest part, followed by a 3-minute rest for whole cuts of pork.
visualDonenessCues: Edges are browned and lightly charred
Surface is sizzling, not wet with raw marinade
foodSafetyNotes: Keep raw pork refrigerated at or below 40°F / 4°C until cooking.
Prevent raw-pork juices and utensils from contacting cooked food or banchan.
Cook whole cuts of pork to at least 145°F / 63°C and rest 3 minutes.
Never operate charcoal, gas, or other fuel-burning grills indoors.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains soy, wheat/gluten, and sesame; verify gochujang and soy sauce labels.

substitutions: Use only verified gluten-free gochujang and tamari for a gluten-free adaptation.
ingredientSourcing: Choose cold skinless pork belly slab from a reputable retailer with intact packaging.
Check every prepared seasoning label for allergens.
makeAhead: Mix marinade up to 2 days ahead; marinate pork only for the stated refrigerated range.
storage: Refrigerate cooked pork in a shallow covered container within 2 hours and use within 4 days pending food-safety approval.
reheating: Reheat only the needed portion to 165°F / 74°C until steaming; avoid repeated reheating.
leftovers: Use properly refrigerated leftovers in rice bowls or lettuce wraps within the approved storage window.
servingSuggestions: Serve in lettuce wraps with fresh vegetables and rice.

faq.question: Why use medium heat?
faq.answer: Gochujang and rice syrup can scorch before thick pork is safely cooked.

faq.question: Can raw marinade be used as sauce?
faq.answer: No. Reserve sauce before raw contact or boil a separate quantity under an approved process.
